title: Tower of Hercules
visualBrief: Granite Roman-core lighthouse with paired recessed facade niches, ascending perimeter band, heavy cornices, two octagonal upper stages, dark lantern and prominent offset stone lightning spine on a polygonal podium.

sourceFacts.basis: A Coruña municipal dimensions, UNESCO identity and inspected 2024 exterior. The 55 m model extent, published hill elevation and mapped height=1 are separate; minor podium/tier dimensions remain reconstruction estimates.

referenceRights: Municipal/UNESCO references retain their own rights. Original2024 photo by Wolfgang Fricke, CC BY3.0, consulted only; no reference image is embedded or redistributed.

nativeAxes.origin: Ground contact below the polygonal podium; +Y up; +Z is the modeled broad landing and entrance-facing elevation, directed northeast (about 59 degrees true); +X faces northwest. The offset staircase/lightning cylinder lies west-northwest of the lantern. The separate narrow northwest podium access is outside this single-landing reconstruction.

geographicProposal.notes: +Y up; +Z is the modeled broad landing and entrance-facing elevation, directed northeast (about 59 degrees true); +X faces northwest. The offset staircase/lightning cylinder lies west-northwest of the lantern. The separate narrow northwest podium access is outside this single-landing reconstruction. Signed quadrant is visually reconstructed from inspected north-up map/aerial access and roof layout, not surveyed camera or entrance azimuth. The square map envelope remains 12.7 m versus the published 11.75 m core; no XY stretch. Platform radius, parapet, minor openings, upper-stage allocation and fittings are photo-proportioned. Host terrain-contact Y=0 is a viewer convention, not the 57 m hill elevation or a surveyed tide/vertical datum. Excavated visitor annex, inscription edicule, separate northwest access, interiors and entire park are not included.

limitations: Original exterior reconstruction from documented main dimensions and inspected references. Individual moldings, sections, weathering, openings and fittings are photo-proportioned estimates.
No interior visitor route, surveyed collision model, operating navigation-light simulation or exact optical assembly is included. Lantern glazing is a restrained opaque PBR approximation.
Shared material references use metric UVs with portable vertex-color PBR fallback. Maximum-fidelity, lit shared-surface and geographic fit reviews remain separate pending gates.

Total55m includes the modeled platform and lightning spine; the allocation among upper tiers and the spine position is photo-estimated. Museum interior, adjacent service structures, terrain, historic excavations and exact lighting installations are omitted.

appearance.identity: Warm granite square Roman-core lighthouse with forty staggered real niches, helical bands, heavy cornice, two octagonal stages, dark lantern and offset stone stair/lightning cylinder.
appearance.master: Original 13060-triangle source master retained byte-for-byte through an isolated leaf recipe; original shared lighthouse module remains unchanged.
appearance.browser: Skyline keeps the polygonal podium with open landing and steps, square shaft and helical bands, two complete upper stages, dark lantern and the full-height offset cylinder. District retains real recessed aperture backs while dropping projecting window trims and reducing regular circular subdivisions. Street and closeup reproduce the complete original exterior.
appearance.epoch: Modern exterior following the 2024 credited photograph; no operative beacon or invented interior.
appearance.exclusions: Signed quadrant is visually reconstructed from inspected north-up map/aerial access and roof layout, not surveyed camera or entrance azimuth. The square map envelope remains 12.7 m versus the published 11.75 m core; no XY stretch. Platform radius, parapet, minor openings, upper-stage allocation and fittings are photo-proportioned. Host terrain-contact Y=0 is a viewer convention, not the 57 m hill elevation or a surveyed tide/vertical datum. Excavated visitor annex, inscription edicule, separate northwest access, interiors and entire park are not included.
